entries.message: Checked workspace, isolated copy clean, HEAD at e32388f. Looked at real engine code before trusting embedded claims.  **Falsified one embedded "verified" claim**: task text claims claim-loop never increments scope's own `Activations` (only ancestors), citing `internal/engine/planning.go` line ~484-487. Read code directly — `planningAncestors(p, scope.ID)` (planning_budget.go:50) includes scope itself as first element before walking to `.Parent`. So `owner.Activations++` loop DOES increment self too. `checkScopeActivation` (planning_budget.go:74) also iterates `planningAncestors` which includes self. Claim doesn't hold against current revision. No code change made for it — false positive, not a prereq blocker for req-11.  **Real state of T3 scope**: grepped for "explor" across `internal/engine/*.go` — zero existing read-only exploration primitive tied to scope/revision. No discovery→task-adaptation persistence path either. Concurrent sub-planning partially exists already (per-scope `Holder`/`Until`/`Generation` lease + optimistic revision check in `planning.go` claim/decide already allows two distinct scope IDs to be claimed independently — that's your req-11 "atomic decisions, distinct scopes" baseline), but nothing implements req-9/10/12 yet. This is greenfield, not a patch.  Scope here (new read-model op + discovery/adaptation persistence + dedup-safe stop/resume + bilingual Mermaid architecture docs + `TestCursorEngineT3*` suite + passing `go test ./internal/engine`) is a multi-file Go feature, not a turn-sized fix. Before I sink budget into a half build I can't finish cleanly:  Want me to (a) continue and implement req-9 (read-only explore op) first as the smallest shippable slice, reporting req-10/11/12 honestly as not_tested/partial, or (b) do the precontrôle/split request to the planner the contract's "next action" field actually asks for (task#N inventory before a big submit)? I won't fabricate PASS on untested criteria either way.
